idiom_name: GObject notifying properties + GtkExpression <binding> in .ui templates (GBinding for two-way)
implementation_notes: C has no language-level observable objects, but the GTK stack supplies the whole mechanism: the view-model is a GObject subclass whose properties emit the notify signal (call g_object_notify_by_pspec from the setter, after the value really changed), the view is a GtkBuilder .ui template whose widget properties are bound to expressions with <binding name='property'><lookup .../></binding>, and g_object_bind_property with G_BINDING_BIDIRECTIONAL gives two-way sync for editable controls. Actions on the same object tree play the command role. Without GTK there is no binder at all: the same design degrades to hand-written structs, function-pointer callbacks and explicit refresh calls (the route embedded toolkits such as LVGL expect), so the library classification applies to GTK/GObject-based C.
pitfalls: Forgetting the notify emission leaves bound widgets stale with no error: GObject only notifies automatically for values set through g_object_set().

.ui <binding> expressions are one-way (expression to property); editable controls need an explicit g_object_bind_property(..., G_BINDING_BIDIRECTIONAL) or a notify handler, or the view-model never sees typing.
A GBinding keeps source and target alive until it is released: unbind with g_binding_unbind() (or drop the returned reference) when a panel is torn down, or the view-model outlives the screen.
Property access and notify must happen on the main-loop thread; notifying from a worker thread is a race - marshal with g_idle_add or GMainContext.
